Oh Hrishikesha, Oh lord of the senses and the god of gods, you, for a long time, in the prison,
having made your mother Devaki, who was made a prisoner, and who was being tormented by the wicked king Kansa, and
with my sons, who were constantly afflicted by calamities, you have freed me. Meaning: Krishna's mother and Kansa's sister Devaki was imprisoned along with her husband Vasudeva in the prison
because the wicked king Kansa was afraid that he would be killed by Devaki's eighth son (Krishna). He had killed all the children of Devakau, who were born before Krishna, but
Krishna escaped from the danger of child sacrifice, because he was delivered to the house of Nand Maharaj, the fosterfather of Lord Krishna. Kunti Devi, along with her sons, continued to be saved from the series of many sufferings.
But Lord Krishna had shown too much favor to Kunti Devi, because
he did not protect Devaki's other sons, while Kunti's sons were protected hl. The reason for this
was that Devaki's husband Vasudev was alive, but Kunti was a widow and besides Krishna
she had no other protector. The conclusion is that Krishna bestows more grace on that devotee who is in greater distress. Sometimes, knowingingly, they put pure devotees into such troubles,
because in such helplessness, the devotee becomes more devoted to God.
The more devotion there is towards God, the more success the devotee will achieve.

Oh Krishna, you have saved us from poisonous food, from terrible fire, from man-eaters,
from wicked assemblies, from the sufferings of exile, and from the war fought by great warriors. And now you have saved us from the weapons of Ashwatthama. Note: The following list of deadly conflicts is presented here. Devaki suffered only once
due to her wicked brother, otherwise she lived comfortably, but Kunti Devi and her
sons had to endure one suffering after another for years. Duryodhana and
his gang kept putting them in trouble for the kingdom, and every time Krishna protected Kunti's sons. Once Bhima was poisoned in the meal. Once, they were kept in the Lakshagriha and set on fire.
And once, Draupadi's garment was taken away, and in the assembly of the wicked Kauravas, they
were humiliated by trying to strip them naked. God fulfilled Draupadi's unlimited
clothes, so that Duryodhana's group could not see her naked.
Similarly, when the five
Pandavas were in exile, Bhima had to fight the man-eating demon Hidimba, but then
God protected Bhima. This game did not end here. After all these sufferings, the great war of Kurukshetra
took place, and Arjuna had to face great warriors like Drona, Bhishma, and Karna. And when everything was finished, Dronacharya's son released a Brahmasra to kill Uttara's unborn child, then God protected the only possible descendant of the Kuru dynasty, Maharaj Parikshit.
